# controlflow

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/controlflow"
```

Package controlflow checks which source paths can reach a branch value.

An if expression can contain return, break, continue, or goto before its final expression. These paths leave the branch without supplying a value. The checker must exclude them when it chooses the result type. Lowering must use the same decision when it emits an assignment to the result variable.

The analysis follows statements and expressions through a graph. Each point has edges to the next possible steps. Return ends a path. Loop exits, labels, and fallthrough have explicit targets. Calls into real function literals keep their own control flow. The checker supplies the meaning of added conditional calls, panic, and unevaluated operands. This package depends only on Go syntax.

## type Result

Result reports whether a branch can reach its last statement or its end.

```go
type Result struct {
    Tail bool
    End  bool
}
```

### func Branch

```go
func Branch(body *ast.BlockStmt, syntax Syntax) Result
```

Branch follows all source paths through a branch. Jumps out of the branch end that path.

## type Syntax

Syntax identifies added conditional calls and calls that cannot return.

```go
type Syntax struct {
    Conditional func(*ast.CallExpr) *ast.IfStmt
    Terminates  func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
    Unevaluated func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
}
```
